rubrics_metrics.name: Autobiography authenticity: literal names, places and events
rubrics_metrics.description: Editor states: 'I am authorized to say that there is not a fictitious name nor place in the whole volume; but that names and places are literally given, and that every transaction therein described actually transpired.' (Editor's Preface)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The editor presents this autobiography as strictly factual; readers and publishers should treat its names, places and transactions as literal and historical rather than fictionalized.

rubrics_metrics.name: Autobiography purpose: emphasize facts over artistic artifice
rubrics_metrics.description: Editor: 'The reader is, therefore, assured, with all due promptitude, that his attention is not invited to a work of ART, but to a work of FACTS—Facts, terrible and almost incredible, it may be yet FACTS, nevertheless.' (Editor's Preface)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Autobiographical writing intended to vindicate social/political principles should prioritize factual accuracy and testimonial force over literary ornament for its own sake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid writing about oneself for mere notoriety; write when it serves a public purpose
rubrics_metrics.description: Douglass (quoted in Editor's Preface) expresses 'repugnance to writing or speaking anything for the public, which could...make me liable to the imputation of seeking personal notoriety' and prefers to write when it will enlighten the public about slavery. (Letter excerpt)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authors should consider motive: autobiographical disclosure is justified when it serves a societal or evidentiary purpose rather than self-aggrandizement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use personal histories as factual evidence to enlighten public opinion on social issues
rubrics_metrics.description: Editor: 'Any facts, either from slaves, slaveholders, or by-standers, calculated to enlighten the public mind, by revealing the true nature, character, and tendency of the slave system, are in order, and can scarcely be innocently withheld.' (Editor's Preface)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personal testimony is valuable in public debate about systemic injustice and should be shared to illuminate institutional realities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Features of strong autobiographical writing: memory, observation, induction, style
rubrics_metrics.description: The editor praises qualities to evaluate the work: 'uncommon memory...keen and accurate insight...original breadth of common sense...a sacred thirst for liberty and for learning...inherent and continuous energy of character...observing, comparing, and careful classifying...descriptive and declamatory powers...style...strength, affluence and terseness...rare polish.' (Introduction and Editor's Preface)
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When assessing an autobiography, consider the author's memory/detail, observational clarity, inductive reasoning from experiences, moral purpose, rhetorical power, and polished but truthful style.
